summary.text: A 57-year-old postmenopausal woman with a past history of irritable bowel syndrome was diagnosed on December 30, 2021 with early-stage invasive ductal carcinoma, Stage 3a, ER positive, PR negative and HER2 negative, with an Oncotype Dx score of 31. She wished to avoid chemotherapy-induced diarrhea and gut microbiota disruption and declined loperamide.

Baseline 16S rRNA stool testing on April 27, 2021 was followed by a personalized prebiotic and probiotic protocol from January 12, 2022, supplements adjusted with the integrative oncologist, a Mediterranean-style diet and exercise advice. She had a double lumpectomy, re-excision and port placement before chemotherapy.

Chemotherapy ran from March 31, 2022 to June 13, 2022 with probiotic blends added the day before and day of infusion, followed by radiation from July 11 to August 11, 2022. Stool samples on March 10 and August 31, 2022 showed shifts in Proteobacteria, Bifidobacterium, butyrate-producing genera and Shannon diversity.

Visits after the first and final chemotherapy infusions recorded no diarrhea or GI symptoms, and at the final visit she reported no further changes to gastrointestinal function including diarrhea and IBS. The authors report no chemotherapy-induced diarrhea, while the patient perspective mentions mild to moderate gut upset for about 24 hours after infusions and no recurrence of IBS.

ambiguities.issue: Surgery date conflict: Table 5 lists the antibiotic at the first surgery as Jan 22, 2022, whereas the microbiota discussion, citing Table 5, lists the first of the three surgeries with antibiotics as January 28, 2022. The second and third dates agree.

ambiguities.issue: Proteobacteria change in March 2022: Table 1 and the April 12 visit text give an increase of 44.58%, while the microbiota section says 69.51% for the same endpoints (1.604% to 2.319%).
